cim: Manchester University Receives $5 Million Artificial Intelligence In Higher Education Grant
cim_eredeti: Manchester University Receives $5 Million Artificial Intelligence In Higher Education Grant
szoveg_eredeti:
NORTH MANCHESTER – Manchester University has received a $5 million grant from Lilly Endowment Inc. to support the development and implementation of approaches for using artificial intelligence.

The grant is made through the Endowment’s initiative, Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education (AIHE), which is helping Indiana colleges and universities respond to AI within their own institutional contexts.

Manchester’s proposal focuses on three priorities: student success and AI fluency, faculty development and curriculum integration, and improvements to operations and data infrastructure.

“This is a significant investment in Manchester’s future and one that will touch nearly every part of the University,” said President Stacy H. Young. “We are grateful to Lilly Endowment Inc. for its commitment to helping Indiana institutions prepare for the opportunities and challenges of artificial intelligence. This grant will allow us to take meaningful steps to integrate AI into teaching, learning and university operations while ensuring our students develop the skills, knowledge and critical thinking needed to thrive in academics and the workforce.”

This initiative is designed to support colleges and universities in Indiana as they develop and implement approaches for using artificial intelligence. The grant will help ensure that Manchester students, faculty and staff are well-equipped to learn, work and live in a world increasingly influenced by AI. Manchester University is one of 35 colleges and universities in Indiana receiving funding through the initiative.

In December 2025, the Endowment awarded Manchester a $125,000 planning grant to support the assessment of the university’s the most compelling needs regarding AI, consideration of the most promising ideas to help address those needs, and preparation for the implementation of grant proposals.
